idiom_name: coordinator struct owning map[ViewID]View under sync.RWMutex + a small View interface
implementation_notes: Go's standard library has neither a GUI nor a view abstraction, so the handler is an ordinary type: a struct holding a map from view handles to a small View interface (Update(*Model), Close()), a mutex around every registry mutation, and a factory map keyed by view type. Notification takes a snapshot of the map values under the lock and releases the lock before calling into views, which is the standard way to avoid both 'concurrent map read and map write' panics and callbacks that re-enter the registry. Fyne supplies the container half when a desktop UI is wanted - container.NewAppTabs/NewStack switch content and fyne.App owns the windows, which must only be touched on its own goroutine via fyne.Do - but it does not provide the model-change fan-out, which stays in the coordinator.
pitfalls: Go maps are not safe for concurrent use: a handler that reads the registry while a UI goroutine adds a view dies with the fatal 'concurrent map read and map write', so both sides must share one mutex.
Calling into views while holding the lock deadlocks as soon as a view opens or closes another view; snapshot the values and release the lock first.
Fyne and similar toolkits are single-goroutine: widget mutation from the coordinator must be dispatched with fyne.Do (or the toolkit's equivalent) instead of running on the notifying goroutine.
Storing interface values keeps every closed view reachable until the entry is deleted, so deletion must be part of Close rather than left to the caller.
